evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction dataset (2014)
evidence.text: The dataset gives 書 as Middle Chinese syo, Old Chinese *s-ta (“write”), and 者 as Middle Chinese tsyaeX, Old Chinese *tAʔ (“nominalizing particle”). The Old Chinese forms do not share the same initial: 書 has *s- and 者 has *t-. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows for both characters match these values. This is a same-system comparison; by itself it does not explain the historical phonetic relationship assigned to 者 in the traditional graph analysis.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.text: The entry reproduces 說文’s analysis of 書 as 箸也, 从聿、者聲, and lists uses for writing, recording, text, book, letter and document with classical examples. The list does not date those uses relative to one another. The dictionary lists the Mandarin reading shū. Several paleographic source tables on the page are marked unavailable.

gaps: The review’s assertion that matched local Baxter–Sagart rows for both characters were unavailable is contradicted by the current task inputs: exact rows are supplied for 書 and 者. The historical phonetic comparison should use these same-system values: MC 書 syo / 者 tsyaeX; OC 書 *s-ta / 者 *tAʔ. Do not claim the OC initials are the same, and avoid overstating how the sound correspondence works.

The official Unicode character-specific lookup pages attempted for 書, 者 and 聿 were inaccessible. The local Unihan readings are supplied data only, not independently verified external records; the opened MOE dictionary independently gives 書 Mandarin shū.
No retrieved primary paleographic source establishes the earliest dated form or an independently dated sequence for 書. The seal graphic page is a modern redraw and was not visually inspected here.

The MOE page lists classical examples for several senses, but dating of textual composition or manuscript witnesses was not established; semantic chronology and links among write, record, text, book, letter and document remain unresolved.
